paragraphs.sourceText: Graphics are used in textbooks as part of the language of the discipline, as in math or economics, or as study aids. Authors use graphic aids to 26 and expand on concepts taken up in the text because graphics are yet another way of portraying relationships and 27 connections.

Graphics are used extensively in natural sciences and social sciences. Social scientists work with statistics 28 data, and the best way to present these statistics is often in graphic form. Graphics are included not merely as a means of making the information easier for the student to grasp, but as an integral part of the way social scientists think. Many textbooks, 29 those in economics, contain appendixes that provide specific information on reading and working with graphic material.

Make it a practice to 30 attentively the titles, captions, headings, and other material connected with graphics. These elements 31 and usually explain what you are looking at. When you are examining graphics, the 32 questions to ask are (a) What is this items about? and (b) What key idea is the author 33 .

One warning: Unless you integrate your reading of graphics with the text, you may make a wrong assumption. 34 , from a chart indicating that 33 percent of firstborn children in a research sample did not feel close to their fathers, you might assume that some dreadful influence was at work on the firstborn children. However, a careful reading of the text 35 that most of the firstborn children in the sample were from single-parent homes in which the father was absent.

paragraphs.sourceText: The Impossibility of Rapid Energy Transitions
paragraphs.translationZh: 快速能量转换的不可能性

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Politicians are fond of promising rapid energy transitions. Whether it is a transition from imported to domestic oil or from coal-powered electricity production to natural-gas power plants, politicians love to talk big. Unfortunately for them (and often the taxpayers), our energy systems are a bit like an aircraft carrier: they are unbelievably expensive, they are built to last for a very long time, they have a huge amount of inertia (meaning it takes a lot of energy to set them moving), and they have a lot of momentum once they are set in motion. No matter how hard you try, you can’t turn something that large on a dime (10 美分硬币）,or even a few thousand dimes.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 政客们热衷于承诺快速的能源转型。无论是从进口石油转向国产石油，还是从燃煤发电转向天然气发电厂，政客们都喜欢说大话。不幸的是，对于他们（通常是纳税人）来说，我们的能源系统有点像一艘航空母舰：它们非常昂贵，它们的建造时间很长，它们有巨大的惯性（意味着需要大量的能量来让它们移动），而且一旦启动它们就有很大的动力。无论你多么努力，你都不可能用一毛钱（10美分硬币），甚至几千毛钱转动那么大的东西。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) In physics, moving objects have two characteristics relevant to understanding the dynamics of energy systems：inertia and momentum. Inertia is the resistance of objects to efforts to change their state of motion. If you try to push a boulder (大圆石）,it pushes you back. Once you have started the boulder rolling, it develops momentum, which is defined by its mass and velocity. Momentum is said to be “conserved,” that is, once you build it up, it has to go somewhere. So a heavy object, like a football player moving at a high speed, has a lot of momentum —that is, once he is moving, it is hard to change his state of motion. If you want to change his course, you have only a few choices: you can stop him, transferring (possibly painfully) some of his kinetic energy (动能) to your own body, or you can approach alongside and slowly apply pressure to gradually alter his course.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 在物理学中，运动物体有两个与理解能量系统动力学相关的特征：惯性和动量。惯性是物体对改变其运动状态的努力的阻力。如果你试图推一块大圆石，它会把你推回去。一旦你开始滚动，它就会产生动量，动量是由它的质量和速度定义的。动量被称为“守恒”，也就是说，一旦你把它推起来，它就必须去某个地方。所以一个重的物体，比如一个高速运动的足球运动员，有很大的动量——也就是说，一旦他开始移动，就很难改变他的运动状态。如果你想改变当他的路线时，你只有几个选择：你可以阻止他，将他的一些动能（动能）转移（可能是痛苦的）到你自己的身体，或者你可以靠近并慢慢施加压力以逐渐改变他的路线。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) But there are other kinds of momentum as well. After all, we don’t speak only of objects or people as having momentum; we speak of entire systems having momentum. Whether it’s a sports team or a presidential campaign, everybody relishes having the big momentum, because it makes them harder to stop or change direction.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 但还有其他类型的动力。毕竟，我们不仅仅谈论具有动量的物体或人；也谈论具有动量的物体或人。我们说整个系统都有动力。无论是运动队还是总统竞选，每个人都喜欢拥有巨大的动力，因为这让他们更难停下来或改变方向。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) One kind of momentum is technological momentum. When a technology is deployed, its impacts reach far beyond itself. Consider the incandescent (白炽灯的）bulb, an object currently hated by many environmentalists and energy-efficiency advocates. The incandescent light bulb, invented by Thomas Edison, which came to be the symbol of inspiration, has been developed into hundreds, if not thousands, of forms. Today, a visit to a lighting store reveals a stunning array of choices. There are standard-shaped bulbs, flame-shaped bulbs, colored globe-shaped bulbs, and more. It is quite easy, with all that choice, to change a light bulb.
paragraphs.translationZh: D）一种动力是技术动力。当一项技术被部署时，其影响远远超出其本身。想想白炽灯，它是目前许多环保主义者和节能倡导者所讨厌的物体。托马斯·爱迪生发明的白炽灯泡后来成为灵感的象征，已经发展成数百种甚至数千种形式。今天，走进一家灯饰店，你会发现令人惊叹的选择。有标准形状的灯泡、火焰形状的灯泡、彩色球形灯泡等等。这很容易。选择，换灯泡。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) But the momentum of incandescent lighting does not stop there. All of those specialized bulbs led to the building of specialized light fixtures, from the desk lamp you study by, to the ugly but beloved hand-painted Chinese lamp you inherited from your grandmother, to the ceiling fixture in your closet, to the light in your oven or refrigerator, and to the light that the dentist points at you. It is easy to change a light bulb, sure, but it is harder to change the bulb and its fixture.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 但白炽灯的发展势头并不止于此。所有这些专用灯泡都催生了专用灯具的建造，从你学习时使用的台灯，到你从祖母那里继承来的丑陋但心爱的手绘中国灯，到你壁橱里的天花板灯具，到你烤箱或冰箱里的灯，再到牙医指着你的灯。当然，更换灯泡很容易，但更换灯泡及其固定装置却很难。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) And there is more to the story, because not only are the devices that house incandescent bulbs shaped to their underlying characteristics, but rooms and entire buildings have been designed in accordance with how incandescent lighting reflects off walls and windows.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 这个故事还有更多内容，因为不仅容纳白炽灯泡的设备是根据其基本特征设计的，而且房间和整个建筑物的设计也是根据白炽灯从墙壁和窗户反射的方式设计的。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) As lighting expert Howard Brandston points out, “Generally, there are no bad light sources, only bad applications.” There are some very commendable characteristics of the CFL [compact fluorescent(焚光的）light bulb], yet the selection of any light source remains inseparable from the luminaire(照明装置）that houses it, along with the space in which both are installed, and lighting requirements that need to be satisfied. The lamp, the fixture, and the room, all three must work in concert for the true benefits of end-users. If the CFL should be used for lighting a particular space, or an object within that space, the fixture must be designed to work with that lamp, and that fixture with the room. It is a symbiotic(共生的） relationship. A CFL cannot be simply installed in an incandescent fixture and then expected to produce a visual appearance that is more than washed out, foggy, and dim. The whole fixture must be replaced —light source and luminaire —and this is never an inexpensive proposition.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 正如照明专家 Howard Brandston 指出的那样，“一般来说，没有不好的光源，只有不好的应用。” CFL [紧凑型荧光灯（焚光的）灯泡] 有一些非常值得称赞的特性，但任何光源的选择仍然与容纳它的照明装置、以及两者安装的空间以及需要满足的照明要求密不可分。灯、灯具和房间，这三者必须协同工作，才能为最终用户带来真正的利益。如果 CFL 应用于照明特定空间或该空间内的物体，则灯具必须设计为与该灯以及该灯具与房间一起使用，这是一种共生的关系。CFL 不能简单地安装在白炽灯灯具中，然后期望产生不仅仅是褪色、雾气和昏暗的视觉外观。必须更换整个灯具——光源和灯具——而这绝不是一个便宜的提议。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) And Brandston knows a thing or two about lighting, being the man who illuminated the Statue of Liberty.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 布兰斯顿对照明略知一二，他是自由女神像的照明者。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Another type of momentum we have to think about when planning for changes in our energy systems is labor-pool momentum. It is one thing to say that we are going to shift 30 percent of our electricity supply from, say, coal to nuclear power in 20 years. But it is another thing to have a supply of trained talent that could let you carry out this promise. That is because the engineers, designers, regulators, operators, and all of the other skilled people needed for the new energy industry are specialists who have to be trained first (or retrained, if they are the ones being laid off in some related industry), and education, like any other complicated endeavor, takes time. And not only do our prospective new energy workers have to be trained, they have to be trained in the right sequence. One needs the designers, and perhaps the regulators, before the builders and operators, and each group of workers in training has to know there is work waiting beyond graduation. In some cases, colleges and universities might have to change their training programs, adding another layer of difficulty.
paragraphs.translationZh: I）在规划能源系统变革时，我们必须考虑的另一种动力是劳动力动力。说我们将在 20 年内将 30% 的电力供应从煤电转向核电是一回事。但拥有训练有素的人才来让你兑现这一承诺又是另一回事了。这是因为新能源行业所需的工程师、设计师、监管者、操作员以及所有其他技术人员都是专家，必须首先接受培训（或者再培训，如果他们是某些相关行业被解雇的人），而教育就像任何其他复杂的工作一样需要时间。我们未来的新能源工人不仅需要接受培训，而且还必须按照正确的顺序接受培训。在建设者和运营商之前，我们需要设计师，也许还需要监管者，而每一组接受培训的工人都必须知道毕业后还有工作等待着。在某些情况下，学院和大学可能不得不改变他们的培训计划，这又增加了一层难度。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) By far the biggest type of momentum that comes into play when it comes to changing our energy systems is economic momentum. The major components of our energy systems, such as fuel production, refining, electrical generation and distribution, are costly installations that have lengthy life spans. They have to operate for long periods of time before the costs of development have been recovered. When investors put up money to build, say, a nuclear power plant, they expect to earn that money back over the planned life of the plant, which is typically between 40 and 60 years. Some coal power plants in the United States have operated for more than 70 years! The oldest continuously operated commercial hydro-electric plant in the United States is on New York’s Hudson River, and it went into commercial service in 1898.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 到目前为止，在改变我们的能源系统方面发挥作用的最大动力是经济动力。我们能源系统的主要组成部分，例如燃料生产、精炼、发电和配电，都是昂贵且使用寿命长的装置。在收回开发成本之前，它们必须运行很长一段时间。例如，当投资者投入资金建造一座核电站时，他们期望在电站的计划寿命（通常为 40 至 60 年）内收回这笔资金。美国一些燃煤电厂已经运行了70多年！美国最古老的持续运营的商业水力发电厂位于纽约哈德逊河，于 1898 年投入商业服务。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) As Vaclav Smil points out, “All the forecasts, plans, and anticipations cited above have failed so miserably because their authors and promoters thought the transitions they hoped to implement would proceed unlike all previous energy transitions, and that their progress could be accelerated in an unprecedented manner.”
paragraphs.translationZh: K）正如瓦茨拉夫·斯米尔（Vaclav Smil）指出的那样，“上面引用的所有预测、计划和预期都惨遭失败，因为它们的作者和推动者认为他们希望实施的转型将不同于以前所有的能源转型，并且它们的进展可以以前所未有的方式加速。”

paragraphs.sourceText: L) When you hear people speaking of making a rapid transition toward any type of energy, whether it is a switch from coal to nuclear power, or a switch from gasoline-powered cars to electric cars, or even a switch from an incandescent to a fluorescent light, understanding energy system inertia and momentum can help you decide whether their plans are feasible.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 当你听到人们谈论向任何类型的能源快速过渡时，无论是从煤炭到核能的转变，还是从汽油动力汽车到电动汽车的转变，甚至是从白炽灯到荧光灯的转变，了解能源系统的惯性和动力可以帮助你确定他们的计划是否可行。

paragraphs.sourceText: 46. Not only moving objects and people but all systems have momentum.
paragraphs.translationZh: 46. 不仅移动的物体和人，而且所有系统都有动量。

paragraphs.sourceText: 47. Changing the current energy system requires the systematic training of professionals and skilled labor.
paragraphs.translationZh: 47. 改变当前的能源体系需要对专业人员和熟练劳动力进行系统培训。

paragraphs.sourceText: 48. Changing a light bulb is easier than changing the fixture housing it.
paragraphs.translationZh: 48. 更换灯泡比更换灯泡更容易。

paragraphs.sourceText: 49. Efforts to accelerate the current energy transitions didn’t succeed as expected,
paragraphs.translationZh: 49. 加速当前能源转型的努力并未取得预期的成功，

paragraphs.sourceText: 50. To change the light source is costly because you have to change the whole fixture.
paragraphs.translationZh: 50. 更换光源的成本很高，因为您必须更换整个灯具。

paragraphs.sourceText: 51. Energy systems, like an aircraft carrier set in motion, have huge momentum.
paragraphs.translationZh: 51. 能源系统就像一艘启航的航空母舰，具有巨大的动力。

paragraphs.sourceText: 52. The problem with lighting, if it arises, often doesn’t lie in light sources but in their applications.
paragraphs.translationZh: 52. 照明问题如果出现，通常不在于光源，而在于其应用。

paragraphs.sourceText: 53. The biggest obstacle to energy transition is that the present energy system is too expensive to replace.
paragraphs.translationZh: 53. 能源转型的最大障碍是现有能源系统的更换成本太高。

paragraphs.sourceText: 54. The application of a technology can impact areas beyond itself.
paragraphs.translationZh: 54. 技术的应用可以影响其本身以外的领域。

paragraphs.sourceText: 55. Physical characteristics of moving objects help explain the dynamics of energy systems.
paragraphs.translationZh: 55. 移动物体的物理特性有助于解释能源系统的动态。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 56 to 60 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 56 至 60 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: One hundred years ago, “Colored” was the typical way of referring to Americans of African descent. Twenty years later, it was purposefully dropped to make way for “Negro.” By the late 1960s, that term was overtaken by “Black.” And then, at a press conference in Chicago in 1988, Jesse Jackson declared that “African American” was the term to embrace. This one was chosen because it echoed the labels of groups, such as “Italian Americans” and “Irish Americans,” that had already been freed of widespread discrimination.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一百年前，“有色人种”是指非裔美国人的典型方式。二十年后，它被故意放弃，为“黑人”让路。到 20 世纪 60 年代末，这个词被“Black”取代。然后，在 1988 年芝加哥举行的新闻发布会上，杰西·杰克逊 (Jesse Jackson) 宣称“非裔美国人”是值得拥抱的词。之所以选择这个，是因为它呼应了“意大利裔美国人”和“爱尔兰裔美国人”等已经摆脱了广泛歧视的群体的标签。

paragraphs.sourceText: A century’s worth of calculated name changes point to the fact that naming any group is a politically freighted exercise. A 2001 study cataloged all the ways in which the term “Black” carried connotations (涵义）that were more negative than those of “African American.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 一个世纪以来精心策划的名称变更表明，为任何团体命名都是一项充满政治色彩的活动。 2001 年的一项研究列出了“黑人”一词所具有的比“非裔美国人”更负面含义的所有方式。

paragraphs.sourceText: But if it was known that “Black” people were viewed differently from “African Americans,” researchers, until now, hadn’t identified what that gap in perception was derived from. A recent study, conducted by Emory University’s Erika Hall, found that “Black” people are viewed more negatively than “African Americans” because of a perceived difference in socioeconomic status. As a result, “Black” people are thought of as less competent and as having colder personalities.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但是，如果知道“黑人”与“非裔美国人”的看法不同，那么研究人员到目前为止还没有确定这种认知差异的根源。埃默里大学埃里卡·霍尔 (Erika Hall) 最近进行的一项研究发现，由于社会经济地位的差异，“黑人”比“非裔美国人”受到更负面的看待。因此，“黑人”被认为能力较差且性格冷漠。

paragraphs.sourceText: The study’s most striking findings shed light on the racial biases permeating the professional world. Even seemingly harmless details on a resume, it appears, can tap into recruiters’ biases. A job application might mention affiliations with groups such as the “Wisconsin Association of African-American Lawyers” or the “National Black Employees Association,” the names of which apparently have consequences, and are also beyond their members’ control.
paragraphs.translationZh: 该研究最引人注目的发现揭示了职业界普遍存在的种族偏见。看来，即使简历上看似无害的细节也可能会利用招聘人员的偏见。求职申请可能会提到与“威斯康星州非裔美国律师协会”或“全国黑人雇员协会”等团体的联系，这些团体的名称显然会产生影响，而且也超出了其成员的控制范围。

paragraphs.sourceText: In one of the study’s experiments, subjects were given a brief description of a man from Chicago with the last name Williams. To one group, he was identified as “African-American,” and another was told he was “Black.” With little else to go on, they were asked to estimate Mr. Williams’s salary, professional standing, and educational background.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在该研究的一项实验中，受试者得到了关于一名来自芝加哥、姓威廉姆斯的男子的简短描述。对于一个群体来说，他被认为是“非裔美国人”，而另一个群体则被告知他是“黑人”。由于没有其他内容可继续，他们被要求估计威廉姆斯先生的薪水、专业地位和教育背景。

paragraphs.sourceText: The “African-American” group estimated that he earned about $ 37 000 a year and had a two-year college degree. The “Black” group, on the other hand, put his salary at about $ 29 000, and guessed that he had only “some” college experience. Nearly three-quarters of the first group guessed that Mr. Williams worked at a managerial level, while only 38.5 percent of the second group thought so.
paragraphs.translationZh: “非裔美国人”团体估计他的年收入约为 37,000 美元，并拥有两年制大学学位。另一方面，“黑人”团体则认为他的工资约为 29,000 美元，并猜测他只有“一些”大学经历。第一组中近四分之三的人猜测威廉姆斯先生从事管理级别的工作，而第二组中只有 38.5% 的人这么认为。

paragraphs.sourceText: Hall’s findings suggest there’s an argument to be made for electing to use “African American,” though one can’t help but get the sense that it’s a decision that papers over the urgency of continued progress. Perhaps a new phrase is needed, one that can bring everyone one big step closer to realizing Du Bois’s original, idealistic hope: “It’s not the name —it’s the Thing that counts.’’ 注意：此部分试题请在答题卡2 上作答。
paragraphs.translationZh: 霍尔的研究结果表明，选择使用“非裔美国人”是有争议的，尽管人们不禁会感觉到，这一决定掩盖了持续进步的紧迫性。也许需要一个新的短语，它可以让每个人离实现杜波依斯最初的理想主义希望又近了一大步：“重要的不是名字，而是事物。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 61 to 65 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 61 至 65 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Across the board, American colleges and universities are not doing a very good job of preparing their students for the workplace or their post-graduation lives. This was made clear by the work of two sociologists, Richard Arum and Josipa Roksa. In 2011 they released a landmark study titled Academically Adrift,” which documented the lack of intellectual growth experienced by many people enrolled in college. In particular, Arum and Roksa found, college students were not developing the critical thinking, analytic reasoning and other higher-level skills that are necessary to thrive in today’s knowledge-based economy and to lead our nation in a time of complex challenges and dynamic change.
paragraphs.translationZh: 总体而言，美国的学院和大学在帮助学生为职场或毕业后生活做好准备方面做得并不好。理查德·阿鲁姆（Richard Arum）和乔西帕·罗克萨（Josipa Roksa）两位社会学家的工作清楚地表明了这一点。 2011年，他们发布了一项名为“学术漂泊”的里程碑式研究，记录了许多大学入学者所经历的智力成长不足的情况。特别是，阿鲁姆和罗克萨发现，大学生没有培养批判性思维、分析推理和其他高级技能，而这些技能是在当今知识经济中蓬勃发展以及在复杂挑战和动态变革时代领导我们国家所必需的。

paragraphs.sourceText: Arum and Roksa placed the blame for students’ lack of learning on a watered-down college curriculum and lowered undergraduate work standards. Although going to college is supposed to be a full-time job, students spent, on average, only 12 to 14 hours a week studying and many were skating through their semesters without doing a significant amount of reading and writing. Students who take more challenging classes and spend more time studying do learn more. But the priorities of many undergraduates are with extracurricular activities, playing sports, and partying and socializing.
paragraphs.translationZh: 阿鲁姆和罗克萨将学生缺乏学习的原因归咎于大学课程的淡化和本科生工作标准的降低。尽管上大学应该是一份全职工作，但学生平均每周只花 12 到 14 个小时学习，而且许多人在整个学期中都在溜冰，没有进行大量的阅读和写作。参加更具挑战性的课程并花更多时间学习的学生确实会学到更多。但许多本科生的首要任务是课外活动、体育运动、聚会和社交。

paragraphs.sourceText: Laura Hamilton, the author of a study on parents who pay for college, will argue in a forthcoming book that college administrations are overly concerned with the social and athletic activities of their students. In Paying for the Party, Hamilton describes what she calls the “party pathway,” which eases many students through college, helped along by various clubs that send students into the party scene and a host of easier majors. By sanctioning this watered-down version of college, universities are “catering to the social and educational needs of wealthy students at the expense of others” who won’t enjoy the financial backing or social connections of richer students once they graduate.
paragraphs.translationZh: 劳拉·汉密尔顿（Laura Hamilton）是一项关于支付大学费用的父母的研究的作者，她将在即将出版的一本书中指出，大学管理部门过度关注学生的社交和体育活动。汉密尔顿在《为派对买单》中描述了她所说的“派对途径”，在各种将学生送入派对场景的俱乐部和许多更容易的专业的帮助下，这种途径可以让许多学生轻松地完成大学学业。通过批准这种淡化版本的大学，大学“以牺牲其他人的利益为代价来满足富裕学生的社会和教育需求”，而这些学生一旦毕业，就无法享受富裕学生的经济支持或社会关系。

paragraphs.sourceText: These students need to build skills and knowledge during college if they are to use their degrees as a stepping-stone to middle-class mobility. But more privileged students must not waste this opportunity either. As recent graduates can testify, the job market isn’t kind to candidates who can’t demonstrate genuine competence, along with a well-cultivated willingness to work hard. Nor is the global economy forgiving of an American workforce with increasingly weak literacy, math and science abilities. College graduates will still fare better than those with only a high school education, of course. But a university degree unaccompanied by a gain in knowledge or skills is an empty achievement indeed. For students who have been coasting through college, and for American universities that have been demanding less work, offering more attractions and charging higher tuition, the party may soon be over. 注意：此部分试题请在答题卡2 上作答。
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果这些学生想利用他们的学位作为中产阶级流动的垫脚石，他们需要在大学期间培养技能和知识。但更有特权的学生也不能浪费这个机会。正如应届毕业生可以证明的那样，就业市场对那些无法表现出真正能力以及良好的努力工作意愿的候选人并不友好。全球经济也无法容忍识字、数学和科学能力日益薄弱的美国劳动力。当然，大学毕业生仍然比那些只受过高中教育的人过得更好。但如果没有知识或技能的增长，大学学位确实是一个空洞的成就。对于那些一直顺利读完大学的学生来说，对于那些要求更少的工作、提供更多景点并收取更高学费的美国大学来说，狂欢可能很快就会结束。
